newsitem.title: UK: RUGBY UNION-NEW-LOOK ENGLAND UNITE AGAINST ITALY.
newsitem.headline: RUGBY UNION-NEW-LOOK ENGLAND UNITE AGAINST ITALY.

text.p: English domestic rugby may be riddled with greed, politics and internecine warfare but on Saturday the factions will come together when a new-look England side takes on Italy at Twickenham.
England have a new captain with Phil de Glanville taking over from Will Carling who, perhaps surprisingly, retained his place in the centre at the expense of Jeremy Guscott.

There are five new caps with full-back Tim Stimpson, wing Adedayo Adebayo and scrumhalf Andy Gomersall coming into the backs while Simon Shaw packs down at lock and Chris Sheasby makes his debut as a late replacement for the injured Ben Clarke.
And just to emphasise the changes, England will be modelling a new shirt, complete for the first time with sponsor's logo.
Whether or not the alterations will mark a change in playing pattern, however, remains to be seen.
De Glanville has been positive so far. "Our general policy is to keep the ball in hand," he said, although the warning signs are there too.
"We are always going to play with options. Not just running the ball all the time, kicking is part of the game too."

What cannot be ignored in the England build-up is the wrangling over players' contracts between the Rugby Football Union and the English Professional Rugby Union Clubs (EPRUC) over the last nine months.

EPRUC's decision to withhold players from early training camps certainly undermined coach Jack Rowell's plans of getting his side properly prepared and, on Thursday, de Glanville admitted that the players felt they were in limbo despite efforts to concentrate on the matter in hand.

"The primary concern is leading the team on the pitch," he stressed. "That is where the difficult decisions have to be made, everything else pales into insignificance against the importance of making the right decisions on the pitch. The acid test comes on Saturday."

Fortress Twickenham suddenly does not seem so secure, especially as the Italians are another factor which cannot be ignored. They have yet to beat England, having lost 36-9 at Twickenham in the 1991 World Cup and only 27-20 in the 1995 edition but their day is fast approaching.
De Glanville, for one, is not taking victory for granted. "They are very streetwise, we can't underestimate them to any extent," he said.

The Italians would sell their grandmothers for a win on Saturday but they know that even if they lose, a good showing would greatly enhance their chances of being admitted to the Five Nations Championship.

They have already scalped Ireland and Scotland and ought to have beaten Wales in Rome recently. They gave the South Africans a tough battle last year and have had a couple of close encounters with the Wallabies.
Certainly de Glanville is in no doubt as to whether they should be in the championship.
"Absolutely, no question," he said. "I think they'll be coming here to prove they should be part of the Five Nations. They're more than capable of beating anyone."

At the heart of the Italians' efforts will be their Durban-born prop Massimo Cuttitta who has selflessly turned down the chance of playing in South Africa and in England in order to help raise the status and standards of the game at home.

Cuttitta missed the loss to Australia in Padua last month because of a thigh injury and ceded the captaincy to flanker Massimo Giovanelli who will again lead the team at Twickenham. But Cuttitta returns to action to win his 50th cap, a milestone shared by the English loosehead Jason Leonard.
De Glanville, though, identifies half-backs Alessandro Troncon and Diego Dominguez as the dangermen.
"Defensively they're very well organised and they're very difficult to break down. They do have a tendency to give away penalties but it's up to us to rise above that and keep our continuity."
The Italians have suffered a couple of reverses, with Massimo Ravazzolo and Diego Scaglia both dropping out through injury.
Teams:

England - 15-Tim Stimpson; 14-Jon Sleightholme, 12-Phil de Glanville (captain), 13-Will Carling, 11-Adedayo Adebayo; 10-Mike Catt, 9-Andy Gomarsall; 8-Chris Sheasby, 7-Tim Rodber, 6-Lawrence Dallaglio, 5-Martin Johnson, 4-Simon Shaw, 3-Graham Rowntree, 2-Mark Regan, 1-Jason Leonard

Italy: 15-Javier Pertile; 14-Paolo Vaccari, 13-Ivan Francescato, 12-Stefano Bordon, 11-Leandro Manteri; 10- Diego Dominguez, 9-Alessandro Troncon; 8-Orazio Arancio, 7-Corrado Covi, 6-Massimo Giovanelli (captain); 5-Carlo Checchinato, 4-Walter Cristofoletto; 3-Franco Properzi Curti, 2-Carlo Orlandi, 1-Massimo Cuttitta.
